meta.title: Finders, keepers? Not in Tokyo
meta.deck: In one of the world's busiest cities, a forgotten umbrella sets off a small civic drama. The system that handles it says a lot about trust.
meta.note: 这是一篇仿《经济学人》风格的原创练习文章，不是真实外刊的转载。文中的事实是概括性描述，仅供语言学习，请不要当作引用来源。

data.title: Finders, keepers? Not in Tokyo

sents.label: 标题
sents.en: Finders, keepers? Not in Tokyo
sents.zh: 捡到就归自己？在东京可不是这样。
notes: finders keepers 是英语俗语（完整版 finders keepers, losers weepers），意思是“谁捡到就归谁”，小孩争东西时常说。
标题用问句加 Not in Tokyo，直接点出反差：东京不吃这一套。

sents.label: 副标题
sents.en: In one of the world's busiest cities, a forgotten umbrella sets off a small civic drama.
sents.zh: 在世界上最繁忙的城市之一，一把被遗忘的雨伞引发了一场小小的市民大戏。
notes: one of the + 最高级 + 复数名词：“最……之一”。
set off：引发、触发。
civic：市民的；a small civic drama 是调侃，把一把雨伞的小事说成“市民大戏”。

sents.label: 副标题
sents.en: The system that handles it says a lot about trust.
sents.zh: 处理这件事的这套体系，很能说明信任是怎么回事。
notes: that handles it 是定语从句，修饰 system，it 指上一句里被遗忘的雨伞。
say a lot about：说明了很多关于……的事情。
让“体系”来“说话”，是新闻英语里常见的拟人写法。

sents.label: 第 1 句
sents.en: Every weekday morning, a small miracle goes largely unnoticed in Tokyo.
sents.zh: 每个工作日的早晨，东京都有一个小小的奇迹发生，却几乎没人留意。
notes: go unnoticed：没被注意到。go + 形容词表示“处于某种状态”，类似 go missing、go wrong。
largely = mostly，基本上。
a small miracle：把小事说成“奇迹”，制造悬念，下一句才揭晓是什么。

sents.label: 第 2 句
sents.en: A commuter slumps onto a train, dozes off, and wakes up one stop too late, minus her umbrella, her scarf or, in the more spectacular cases, an envelope stuffed with cash.
sents.zh: 一位通勤者瘫坐在电车上，打起瞌睡，醒来时已经坐过了一站，少了一把伞、一条围巾，更夸张的情况下，还少了一个塞满现金的信封。
notes: 主干是三个并列谓语：slumps onto、dozes off、wakes up。
slump onto：瘫坐在……上；doze off：打瞌睡；stuffed with：塞满。
one stop too late：晚了一站，也就是睡过站。
minus 在这里是介词，“少了……”，口语化的幽默用法，表示醒来时东西没了。
in the more spectacular cases 是插入语；spectacular 本义“壮观的”，这里是反语，指更离谱的情况。

sents.label: 第 3 句
sents.en: By the time she has finished cursing, the item has often begun an improbable journey.
sents.zh: 等她骂完的时候，那件东西往往已经踏上了一段出人意料的旅程。
notes: by the time + 从句：“等到……的时候”。主句用现在完成时 has begun，表示到那时旅程已经开始。
finish doing sth.：finish 后面接动名词，所以是 finished cursing。
cursing：咒骂、骂脏话，这里指懊恼地发泄几句。
improbable：不太可能的，出人意料的。journey 把物品拟人化，引出下一句的流转路线。

sents.label: 第 4 句
sents.en: It goes from a station attendant's desk to a neighbourhood police box and, if nobody comes forward, to a central lost-property office, where it is logged, labelled and stored.
sents.zh: 它先从车站工作人员的桌上转到街区的交番，如果没人来认领，再转到中央失物招领处，在那里被登记、贴标签、存放起来。
notes: goes from A to B and ... to C：一路写出物品的流转路径。
if nobody comes forward：come forward 是“站出来（认领、作证）”。
where it is logged, labelled and stored：where 引导非限制性定语从句，修饰 office；三个被动动词并列，节奏感强。logged 是 log 的过去分词，“登记在案”。
police box 就是日本的交番（koban），后文会再出现。lost-property office 是英式说法，美式常说 lost and found。
neighbourhood、labelled 是英式拼写，美式是 neighborhood、labeled。

sents.label: 第 5 句
sents.en: The scale is staggering.
sents.zh: 规模之大，令人吃惊。
notes: staggering：令人震惊的，常形容数量或规模大。
上一句是长句，这里用一个短句收束，再展开数字，是英文评论文常见的节奏处理。

sents.label: 第 6 句
sents.en: Police in the capital handle several million lost items a year.
sents.zh: 首都的警方每年要处理好几百万件遗失物品。
notes: the capital 指东京，避免重复 Tokyo。
several million：好几百万，million 前面有 several 时不加 s。
a year = per year，这里的 a 表示“每”。

sents.label: 第 7 句
sents.en: By sheer volume, umbrellas lead the pack, yet almost nobody comes to claim them; a cheap umbrella is the one possession Tokyoites seem happy to lose.
sents.zh: 单论数量，雨伞遥遥领先，但几乎没人来认领；便宜的雨伞，似乎是东京人唯一乐意丢掉的东西。
notes: by sheer volume：单凭数量；sheer 表示“纯粹的”，起强调作用。
lead the pack：遥遥领先（pack 指赛跑里的大部队）。
yet 表转折，比 but 更正式；claim 在这里是“认领”。
分号连接两个相关的分句。the one possession (that) Tokyoites seem happy to lose 省略了关系代词 that；Tokyoites 是东京人。

sents.label: 第 8 句
sents.en: Wallets are another story.
sents.zh: 钱包就另当别论了。
notes: X is another story：固定表达，“X 则另当别论”。
同类说法：that's a different story、that's another matter。
短句转折，把话题从雨伞切到钱包。

sents.label: 第 9 句
sents.en: A striking share of them find their way back to their owners, cash and all.
sents.zh: 其中相当大一部分都找到了回到失主手里的路，连里面的现金也一分不少。
notes: a striking share of them：striking 是“显著的”，share 是“份额”；them 指钱包。谓语用复数 find，是按意义一致（them 是复数）。
find their way back to：找到回去的路，拟人手法，呼应前面的 journey。
cash and all：连现金在内也一样，and all 是口语用法，表示“连同……一起”。

sents.label: 第 10 句
sents.en: Economists would start with incentives.
sents.zh: 经济学家会先从激励机制说起。
notes: would + 动词原形：表示“通常会这样做”，描述典型行为。
incentives：激励、诱因，经济学里的基本概念。
作者先借经济学家的视角起头，下一句马上给出具体的激励机制。

sents.label: 第 11 句
sents.en: Japanese law obliges finders to hand in what they pick up, and entitles them to a reward of between 5% and 20% of the item's value, payable by the owner.
sents.zh: 日本法律要求拾得者上交捡到的东西，同时赋予他们获得物品价值 5% 到 20% 报酬的权利，由失主支付。
notes: oblige sb. to do sth.：责成某人做某事；entitle sb. to sth.：赋予某人……的权利。前者是义务，后者是权利，两个动词共用主语 law，对比工整。
hand in：上交。what they pick up 是名词性从句，作 hand in 的宾语。
a reward of between 5% and 20% of the item's value：价值为物品价值 5% 到 20% 的报酬。
payable by the owner：形容词短语后置，修饰 reward，“由失主支付”。

sents.label: 第 12 句
sents.en: In practice, many finders reportedly waive it.
sents.zh: 实际上，据说许多拾得者放弃了这笔报酬。
notes: in practice：实际上（对应 in theory，理论上）。
reportedly：据报道、据说，说明信息是转述的，作者不为其担保，新闻文体常用。
waive：放弃（权利、费用）。it 指上一句的 reward。

sents.label: 第 13 句
sents.en: Incentives, then, explain only part of the story.
sents.zh: 这么看来，激励只能解释这个故事的一部分。
notes: then 放在主语后面作插入语，表示“那么，由此看来”，语气比放在句首更含蓄。
only part of the story：只解释了一部分，为下文的 infrastructure and habit 铺垫。

sents.label: 第 14 句
sents.en: The rest lies in infrastructure and habit.
sents.zh: 其余的原因在于配套机制和习惯。
notes: the rest：其余部分。
lie in：在于，表示原因或关键所在。
infrastructure：本义是基础设施，这里引申为配套的设施和制度；habit 是民众的行为习惯。一个偏“硬”，一个偏“软”。

sents.label: 第 15 句
sents.en: The koban, the small police boxes found in nearly every neighbourhood, make doing the right thing cheap: there is almost always one within a short walk.
sents.zh: 交番，也就是几乎每个街区都有的小型派出所，让做正确的事变得成本很低：走几步路，几乎总能找到一个。
notes: The koban, the small police boxes ... 是同位语，解释 koban；found in nearly every neighbourhood 是过去分词作后置定语。koban 单复数同形，所以这里谓语用 make。
make doing the right thing cheap：make + 宾语 + 形容词；宾语是动名词短语，cheap 指成本低，不是价格便宜。
冒号后面补充说明：几乎总有一个在步行很短的距离内（within a short walk）。

sents.label: 第 16 句
sents.en: The process itself is gloriously dull, a form, a receipt, a database entry.
sents.zh: 整个流程本身乏味得恰到好处：填一张表，拿一张收据，录入一条数据。
notes: gloriously dull：反语式夸赞。dull 本是贬义，但这里的“无聊”正是优点：简单、没有麻烦。
逗号后面三个名词并列（a form, a receipt, a database entry），列出流程的具体内容，没有 and，节奏利落。
the process itself：itself 强调“流程本身”。

sents.label: 第 17 句
sents.en: Social scientists might call this lowering the cost of honesty.
sents.zh: 社会科学家或许会把这称为降低诚实的成本。
notes: might call this ...：might 让语气更谦逊，“或许会称之为”。
call A B：把 A 称为 B，这里 B 是动名词短语 lowering the cost of honesty。
the cost of honesty：把诚实看作要付成本的事，是经济学的思路，也是全文的核心比喻。

sents.label: 第 18 句
sents.en: It is a lesson that travels.
sents.zh: 这是一条可以推广到别处的经验。
notes: a lesson that travels：that 引导定语从句；travel 在这里指“可以被带到别处适用”。
短句，承上启下，从东京的个案转向更普遍的结论。
It 指前面说的“降低诚实的成本”这个道理。

sents.label: 第 19 句
sents.en: A much-cited experiment published in Science in 2019 left thousands of "lost" wallets at hotels, banks and offices in 40 countries.
sents.zh: 2019 年发表在《科学》杂志上的一项被广泛引用的实验，在 40 个国家的酒店、银行和办公室里留下了数千个“遗失”的钱包。
notes: much-cited：复合形容词（副词 + 过去分词），被大量引用的。
published in Science in 2019：过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 experiment。Science 是期刊名。
“lost”加了引号，因为钱包是研究者故意留下的，并不是真的丢了。
thousands of：数以千计的。

sents.label: 第 20 句
sents.en: Counterintuitively, wallets containing more money were more likely to be returned, not less.
sents.zh: 违反直觉的是，装钱更多的钱包反而更有可能被送还，而不是更不可能。
notes: counterintuitively：句首副词，修饰整句，“违反直觉的是”。
containing more money：现在分词短语作后置定语，修饰 wallets。
not less：省略了 likely to be returned，完整说法是 not less likely to be returned。

sents.label: 第 21 句
sents.en: The researchers' explanation was that people dislike seeing themselves as thieves, and that this feeling grows with the size of the temptation.
sents.zh: 研究者的解释是，人们不喜欢把自己看成小偷，而且这种感觉会随着诱惑的大小而增强。
notes: The researchers' explanation was that ...：主系表结构，that 引导表语从句；后面 and that this feeling grows ... 是并列的第二个 that 从句。
dislike doing sth.：不喜欢做某事；see oneself as：把自己看作。
grow with the size of the temptation：随诱惑的大小而增强。
researchers' 是复数所有格，撇号在 s 后。

sents.label: 第 22 句
sents.en: Honesty, in other words, is not merely a personal virtue.
sents.zh: 换句话说，诚实不只是一种个人美德。
notes: in other words：换句话说，用来引出总结。
not merely：不仅仅，暗示后面还有一层意思，下一句的 also 就接上了。
virtue：美德。

sents.label: 第 23 句
sents.en: It is also a service that a society either provides or fails to provide.
sents.zh: 它也是一种服务，社会要么提供，要么没能提供。
notes: a service that a society either provides or fails to provide：that 引导定语从句，在从句中作 provides 和 fails to provide 的宾语。
either ... or ...：连接两个并列谓语。
fail to provide 比 not provide 更像“想做却没做到”，略带批评意味。

sents.label: 第 24 句
sents.en: When the cost of doing the right thing falls to nearly zero, most people do it; when it does not, no amount of moral exhortation will fill the gap.
sents.zh: 当做正确的事的成本降到几乎为零，大多数人都会去做；当成本降不下来，再多的道德劝诫也填补不了这个缺口。
notes: 两个 when 从句对称，用分号隔开：成本降下来，人们就去做；成本降不下来，说教也没用。
when it does not：省略了 fall to nearly zero，避免重复。
no amount of ... will ...：强调否定，“再多的……也不会……”。
exhortation：劝诫、规劝；fill the gap：填补缺口。
the cost of doing the right thing 呼应第 17 句的 cost of honesty。

sents.label: 第 25 句
sents.en: Meanwhile, the umbrellas pile up in Iidabashi, a quiet monument to the one thing Tokyo cannot legislate: the rain.
sents.zh: 与此同时，雨伞在饭田桥越堆越多，成了一座安静的纪念碑，纪念东京唯一无法立法规定的东西：雨。
notes: meanwhile：与此同时，把话题从道理拉回到画面。
pile up：堆积。Iidabashi（饭田桥）是东京的地名，东京警视厅的遗失物中心在那一带。
a quiet monument to ...：同位语，指“雨伞堆积”这件事像一座安静的纪念碑；monument to 是“……的纪念碑”。
the one thing (that) Tokyo cannot legislate：省略了 that；legislate 是立法规定。冒号后点题：the rain。雨是法律管不了的，结尾幽默，也和开头的雨伞首尾呼应。

vocab.ctx: A commuter slumps onto a train, dozes off, and wakes up one stop too late

ex.en: After the night shift, he [[slumped onto]] the sofa and fell asleep at once.
ex.zh: 上完夜班，他一屁股瘫坐在沙发上，立刻睡着了。

ex.en: The exhausted hikers [[slumped onto]] the grass at the top of the hill.
ex.zh: 筋疲力尽的徒步者们瘫坐在山顶的草地上。

vocab.ctx: A commuter slumps onto a train, dozes off, and wakes up one stop too late

ex.en: I kept [[dozing off]] during the boring lecture.
ex.zh: 那堂课太无聊，我一直在打瞌睡。

ex.en: Grandpa [[dozed off]] in front of the TV again.
ex.zh: 爷爷又在电视机前打起了瞌睡。

vocab.ctx: an envelope stuffed with cash

ex.en: The suitcase was [[stuffed with]] gifts for her family.
ex.zh: 行李箱里塞满了给家人的礼物。

ex.en: His inbox is [[stuffed with]] unread emails.
ex.zh: 他的收件箱里塞满了没读的邮件。

vocab.zh: 不太可能的，出人意料的
vocab.ctx: the item has often begun an improbable journey

ex.en: It seems [[improbable]] that anyone would ignore such an offer.
ex.zh: 有人会无视这样的提议，这似乎不太可能。

ex.en: The two friends met again in the most [[improbable]] place: a tiny airport in Iceland.
ex.zh: 两个朋友在最出人意料的地方重逢了：冰岛的一个小机场。

vocab.ctx: if nobody comes forward, to a central lost-property office

ex.en: Police have asked witnesses to [[come forward]].
ex.zh: 警方呼吁目击者站出来。

ex.en: Nobody [[came forward]] to claim the lost bag.
ex.zh: 没有人出面来认领那个丢失的包。

vocab.ctx: The scale is staggering.

ex.en: The cost of the project is [[staggering]].
ex.zh: 这个项目的成本高得惊人。

ex.en: She won the race by a [[staggering]] margin.
ex.zh: 她以惊人的优势赢得了比赛。

vocab.ctx: By sheer volume, umbrellas lead the pack

ex.en: The company drowned its rivals [[by sheer volume]], shipping ten times more products.
ex.zh: 这家公司单凭数量就压倒了对手，出货量是对方的十倍。

ex.en: [[By sheer volume]], English dominates academic publishing.
ex.zh: 单从数量上看，英语在学术出版中占据主导。

vocab.ctx: By sheer volume, umbrellas lead the pack

ex.en: Japan's bullet trains [[lead the pack]] on punctuality.
ex.zh: 在准点率方面，日本的新干线遥遥领先。

ex.en: Her start-up has begun to [[lead the pack]] in clean energy.
ex.zh: 她的初创公司已经开始在清洁能源领域领跑。

vocab.ctx: Wallets are another story.

ex.en: Cooking pasta is easy. Making it from scratch is [[another story]].
ex.zh: 煮意面很简单，从头自己做就是另一回事了。

ex.en: He plays the piano well, but singing is [[another story]].
ex.zh: 他钢琴弹得不错，唱歌就另当别论了。

vocab.ctx: entitles them to a reward of between 5% and 20% of the item's value

ex.en: A valid ticket [[entitles]] you to a free drink.
ex.zh: 有效门票可以让你免费领取一杯饮料。

ex.en: Employees are [[entitled to]] four weeks of paid leave.
ex.zh: 员工有权享受四周带薪假期。

vocab.ctx: In practice, many finders reportedly waive it.

ex.en: The bank agreed to [[waive]] the late fee.
ex.zh: 银行同意免除滞纳金。

ex.en: Students may [[waive]] the fee if they show proof of low income.
ex.zh: 学生如果能出示低收入证明，可以免交这项费用。

vocab.zh: 基础设施；这里引申为配套机制
vocab.ctx: The rest lies in infrastructure and habit.

ex.en: The country is investing heavily in transport [[infrastructure]].
ex.zh: 这个国家正在大力投资交通基础设施。

ex.en: Good ideas fail without the [[infrastructure]] to support them.
ex.zh: 没有配套机制的支撑，再好的点子也会落空。

vocab.zh: 乏味得恰到好处（反语式夸赞）
vocab.ctx: The process itself is gloriously dull, a form, a receipt, a database entry.

ex.en: The meeting was [[gloriously dull]]: nothing went wrong, and nothing happened.
ex.zh: 那场会议乏味得恰到好处：没出任何岔子，也什么都没发生。

ex.en: After a chaotic year, he longed for a [[gloriously dull]] weekend at home.
ex.zh: 经历了混乱的一年，他渴望在家过一个平平淡淡的周末。

vocab.zh: 可以推广到别处的经验
vocab.ctx: It is a lesson that travels.

ex.en: Tokyo's lost-property system is [[a lesson that travels]]: any city could copy it.
ex.zh: 东京的失物招领体系是一个可以推广的经验：任何城市都能照搬。

ex.en: Her approach to teaching is [[a lesson that travels]] across subjects.
ex.zh: 她的教学方法是一条可以推广到各个学科的经验。

vocab.ctx: Counterintuitively, wallets containing more money were more likely to be returned, not less.

ex.en: [[Counterintuitively]], students who rested more scored higher.
ex.zh: 违反直觉的是，休息得更多的学生分数反而更高。

ex.en: [[Counterintuitively]], a smaller team often finishes the project faster.
ex.zh: 违反直觉的是，人少的团队往往完成项目更快。

vocab.ctx: no amount of moral exhortation will fill the gap

ex.en: No [[exhortation]] from the coach could lift the team's spirits.
ex.zh: 教练再怎么规劝也提振不了队伍的士气。

ex.en: The speech was a long [[exhortation]] to work harder.
ex.zh: 这场演讲是一番冗长的规劝，要大家更加努力。

vocab.zh: 立法规定；这里指靠法律管控
vocab.ctx: the one thing Tokyo cannot legislate: the rain

ex.en: You cannot [[legislate]] good manners.
ex.zh: 礼貌是没法靠立法规定出来的。

ex.en: Parliament plans to [[legislate]] against fake reviews.
ex.zh: 议会打算立法禁止虚假评价。

vocab.zh: 咒骂，骂脏话；懊恼地发泄几句
vocab.ctx: By the time she has finished cursing, the item has often begun an improbable journey.

ex.en: He stubbed his toe and began [[cursing]] under his breath.
ex.zh: 他踢到了脚趾，低声咒骂起来。

ex.en: She [[cursed]] the rain when her umbrella blew inside out.
ex.zh: 伞被风吹翻的时候，她咒骂起这场雨。

vocab.ctx: a central lost-property office, where it is logged, labelled and stored

ex.en: Every complaint is [[logged]] in the system.
ex.zh: 每一条投诉都会登记在系统里。

ex.en: The nurse [[logged]] the patient's temperature every hour.
ex.zh: 护士每小时记录一次病人的体温。

vocab.zh: 责成某人做某事；（法律上）要求某人必须……
vocab.ctx: Japanese law obliges finders to hand in what they pick up

ex.en: The law [[obliges]] employers to provide a safe workplace.
ex.zh: 法律要求雇主提供安全的工作场所。

ex.en: Drivers are [[obliged]] to stop at a red light.
ex.zh: 司机必须在红灯前停车。

vocab.zh: 服务人员；station attendant 是站务员
vocab.ctx: It goes from a station attendant's desk to a neighbourhood police box

ex.en: A station [[attendant]] helped her find the right platform.
ex.zh: 一位站务员帮她找到了正确的站台。

ex.en: The flight [[attendant]] offered us tea.
ex.zh: 空乘人员给我们递上了茶。

vocab.ctx: a reward of between 5% and 20% of the item's value, payable by the owner
vocab.note: 常见搭配：payable by sb. 由某人支付 / payable to sb. 付给某人 / payable on delivery 货到付款 / payable in installments 分期付款 / payable within 30 days 须在 30 天内支付

ex.en: The fee is [[payable]] within 30 days.
ex.zh: 这笔费用须在 30 天内支付。

ex.en: Cheques should be made [[payable]] to the university.
ex.zh: 支票请开成以学校为收款人。

ex.en: The balance is [[payable]] on delivery.
ex.zh: 余款货到付款。

vocab.zh: adj. 壮观的；惊人的；（情况）更离谱的
vocab.ctx: A commuter slumps onto a train, dozes off, and wakes up one stop too late, minus her umbrella, her scarf or, in the more spectacular cases, an envelope stuffed with cash.
vocab.note: in the more spectacular cases：在更夸张、更离谱的情况下

ex.en: The fireworks over Tokyo Bay were [[spectacular]].
ex.zh: 东京湾上空的烟花美不胜收。

ex.en: The start-up's growth was [[spectacular]]; so was its collapse.
ex.zh: 这家初创公司的增长惊人，垮台也同样惊人。

ex.en: In the more [[spectacular]] cases, the fraud ran for a decade before anyone noticed.
ex.zh: 在更离谱的案例中，骗局持续了十年才被人发觉。

vocab.ctx: Finders, keepers? Not in Tokyo
vocab.note: 出自儿童顺口溜 “Finders keepers, losers weepers”（捡到的归自己，丢了的只能哭）。标题是反用：在东京，不是这样。

ex.en: I found a ten-pound note on the bus, and my brother grinned: “[[Finders, keepers]]!”
ex.zh: 我在公交车上捡到一张十英镑的钞票，我弟弟咧嘴一笑：“谁捡到归谁！”

ex.en: Children chant “[[finders keepers]], losers weepers” in the playground, but the law is less forgiving.
ex.zh: 孩子们在操场上念着“捡到归己，丢了活该”，但法律就没这么宽容了。

ex.en: He took a “[[finders, keepers]]” attitude to the abandoned bike until its owner turned up.
ex.zh: 他对那辆被丢弃的自行车抱着“谁捡到归谁”的态度，直到车主出现。

vocab.zh: adj. 市民的；公民的；城市的
vocab.ctx: In one of the world's busiest cities, a forgotten umbrella sets off a small civic drama.
vocab.note: 常见搭配：civic duty 公民义务 / civic pride 城市自豪感 / civic life 公共生活

ex.en: Many people see voting as a [[civic]] duty.
ex.zh: 很多人把投票看作公民的义务。

ex.en: The town hall is the centre of [[civic]] life.
ex.zh: 市政厅是这座城市公共生活的中心。

ex.en: Residents showed real [[civic]] pride after the park was restored.
ex.zh: 公园修复之后，居民们表现出强烈的城市自豪感。

vocab.zh: adv. 基本上；主要地；大体上
vocab.ctx: Every weekday morning, a small miracle goes largely unnoticed in Tokyo.
vocab.note: largely unnoticed：基本没人注意到。别和形容词 large 搞混。

ex.en: The report was [[largely]] ignored by the press.
ex.zh: 这份报告基本上被媒体忽视了。

ex.en: The delay was [[largely]] due to bad weather.
ex.zh: 这次延误主要是因为天气不好。

ex.en: The city is [[largely]] safe, though a few areas need caution.
ex.zh: 这座城市基本上是安全的，不过有几个区域需要小心。

vocab.ctx: A commuter slumps onto a train, dozes off, and wakes up one stop too late, minus her umbrella, her scarf or, in the more spectacular cases, an envelope stuffed with cash.
vocab.note: 句型：one + 时间/距离单位 + too late，表示“晚了那么一点”。

ex.en: I fell asleep on the Yamanote Line and woke up [[one stop too late]].
ex.zh: 我在山手线上睡着了，醒来时已经坐过了一站。

ex.en: She noticed the announcement [[one stop too late]] and had to double back.
ex.zh: 她听到广播时已经过了一站，只好折返。

ex.en: We got off [[one stop too late]] and had to take a taxi back.
ex.zh: 我们下车晚了一站，只好打车回去。

vocab.zh: prep. 少了……；没有了……（口语化）
vocab.ctx: A commuter slumps onto a train, dozes off, and wakes up one stop too late, minus her umbrella, her scarf or, in the more spectacular cases, an envelope stuffed with cash.
vocab.note: 口语里常带幽默或无奈，暗示“本该有却没了”。数学里的 minus 才是“减”。

ex.en: He came back from holiday [[minus]] his luggage.
ex.zh: 他度假回来了，行李却丢了。

ex.en: She walked in, [[minus]] her usual smile.
ex.zh: 她走了进来，脸上少了往常的笑容。

ex.en: We arrived at the party [[minus]] the cake, which was still in the car.
ex.zh: 我们到了聚会现场，蛋糕却没带来——它还留在车里。

vocab.ctx: By the time she has finished cursing, the item has often begun an improbable journey.
vocab.note: by the time 后接从句；主句常用完成时，表示“到那时已经……”。

ex.en: [[By the time]] I reached the station, the last train had gone.
ex.zh: 我赶到车站时，末班车已经开走了。

ex.en: [[By the time]] you read this, I will have landed in Shanghai.
ex.zh: 等你读到这条消息的时候，我应该已经降落在上海了。

ex.en: [[By the time]] the police arrived, the thief had disappeared.
ex.zh: 警察赶到的时候，小偷已经不见了。

vocab.ctx: By sheer volume, umbrellas lead the pack, yet almost nobody comes to claim them; a cheap umbrella is the one possession Tokyoites seem happy to lose.
vocab.note: 指随身物品时多用复数 possessions；in possession of ……：持有、拥有。

ex.en: Her most treasured [[possession]] is an old camera from her grandfather.
ex.zh: 她最珍视的物品是祖父留下的一台旧相机。

ex.en: Passengers are asked to keep their [[possessions]] with them at all times.
ex.zh: 请乘客随时随身携带好个人物品。

ex.en: The police found him in [[possession]] of a stolen wallet.
ex.zh: 警方发现他持有一个被盗的钱包。

vocab.ctx: A striking share of them find their way back to their owners, cash and all.
vocab.note: 名词 + and all，放在句末，表示“连带着也一起”。

ex.en: She swallowed the sandwich, crust [[and all]].
ex.zh: 她把三明治整个吞了下去，连面包边也不剩。

ex.en: He fell into the river, phone [[and all]].
ex.zh: 他掉进了河里，连手机也一起掉了进去。

ex.en: They bought the old house, furniture [[and all]].
ex.zh: 他们买下了那栋老房子，家具也一并带走。

vocab.zh: 上交；提交（作业、失物、辞呈等）
vocab.ctx: Japanese law obliges finders to hand in what they pick up, and entitles them to a reward of between 5% and 20% of the item's value, payable by the owner.
vocab.note: 可以拆开用：hand it in。hand in 偏“交上去”，hand over 偏“移交”。

ex.en: Please [[hand in]] your essays by Friday.
ex.zh: 请在周五之前交上论文。

ex.en: She [[handed in]] the lost wallet at the nearest police box.
ex.zh: 她把捡到的钱包交给了最近的警亭。

ex.en: He [[handed in]] his notice last week.
ex.zh: 他上周递交了辞呈。

vocab.zh: 事实上；实际上（对比：in theory 理论上）
vocab.ctx: In practice, many finders reportedly waive it.
vocab.note: 常和 in theory 成对出现：理论上如何，实际上却不一定。

ex.en: In theory the system is simple; [[in practice]], it takes hours.
ex.zh: 理论上这个系统很简单，实际操作起来却要花好几个小时。

ex.en: The rule applies to everyone, but [[in practice]] it is rarely enforced.
ex.zh: 这条规定对所有人适用，但实际上很少被执行。

ex.en: [[In practice]], most people just click “accept” without reading.
ex.zh: 实际上，大多数人根本不看就点了“同意”。

vocab.ctx: In practice, many finders reportedly waive it.
vocab.note: 消息来自报道或传闻，作者并没有亲自核实，新闻里很常见。

ex.en: The singer has [[reportedly]] cancelled her tour.
ex.zh: 据报道，这位歌手已经取消了巡演。

ex.en: The company [[reportedly]] lost millions last year.
ex.zh: 据说这家公司去年亏损了数百万。

ex.en: He was [[reportedly]] furious when he heard the news.
ex.zh: 据说他听到消息时非常愤怒。

vocab.ctx: The rest lies in infrastructure and habit.
vocab.note: lie（位于；在于）的变形是 lie – lay – lain，三单 lies；撒谎的 lie 过去式才是 lied。

ex.en: The secret of her success [[lies in]] hard work, not talent.
ex.zh: 她成功的秘诀在于努力，而不是天赋。

ex.en: The problem [[lies in]] how the data is collected.
ex.zh: 问题出在数据的收集方式上。

ex.en: The charm of the old town [[lies in]] its narrow streets.
ex.zh: 这座老城的魅力就在于那些狭窄的街道。

vocab.ctx: Honesty, in other words, is not merely a personal virtue.
vocab.note: 比 not only 更书面；常见结构 not merely A but (also) B。

ex.en: The museum is [[not merely]] a building but a living archive.
ex.zh: 这座博物馆不仅仅是一栋建筑，更是一座活的档案馆。

ex.en: It is [[not merely]] a matter of money.
ex.zh: 这不仅仅是钱的问题。

ex.en: She is [[not merely]] talented; she is also relentlessly disciplined.
ex.zh: 她不仅仅有天赋，还自律得近乎苛刻。

vocab.ctx: Honesty, in other words, is not merely a personal virtue.
vocab.note: by virtue of ……：凭借、由于（较正式）。

ex.en: Patience is a [[virtue]].
ex.zh: 耐心是一种美德。

ex.en: The plan's main [[virtue]] is its simplicity.
ex.zh: 这个方案最大的优点就是简单。

ex.en: She got the job [[by virtue of]] her experience, not her connections.
ex.zh: 她得到这份工作是凭借经验，而不是人脉。

vocab.ctx: When the cost of doing the right thing falls to nearly zero, most people do it; when it does not, no amount of moral exhortation will fill the gap.
vocab.note: amount 后面接不可数名词；后半句常用 will / can。

ex.en: [[No amount of]] apologies will undo the damage.
ex.zh: 再多的道歉也无法挽回这些损失。

ex.en: [[No amount of]] coffee will make me enjoy Monday mornings.
ex.zh: 再多的咖啡也不会让我爱上周一的早晨。

ex.en: [[No amount of]] training will make up for a lack of curiosity.
ex.zh: 再多的训练也弥补不了好奇心的缺失。

breakdown.en: When the cost of doing the right thing falls to nearly zero, most people do it; when it does not, no amount of moral exhortation will fill the gap.
points: 结构是两个并列的 when 从句加主句，前后对比。
第二个 when 后的 it does not 省略了 fall to nearly zero，避免重复。
no amount of... will... 是强调否定的固定搭配，意思是“再多的……也无法……”。
fill the gap 指弥补这个缺口，即成本过高时靠道德说教填不上。

questions: 作者认为“诚实”主要是个人品质，还是社会提供的一种服务？哪些句子支持这个判断？
结尾 “the one thing Tokyo cannot legislate: the rain” 用了什么修辞效果？
用 by sheer volume、another story、counterintuitively 各造一个关于你自己领域（比如政治经济）的句子。
